scopeChangeReason: Three exclusions, each for a stated reason rather than convenience. The watchdog-budget files carry a separate config-derived-versus-generic-default asymmetry that two decision documents already record as an independently owned subsystem; merging it here would produce one unreviewable change out of two independent defects. The process-fact files are excluded per OQ-B3434-1: bounding the serialised artifact introduces no new process fact, and if an implementer finds otherwise that is a real expansion to raise explicitly. Separately recorded rather than silently ignored: the scope reviewer identified done-required-evidence.json, written by the doneRequiredCommands runner rather than by handlers/verifier.ts, as carrying the IDENTICAL per-command aggregate growth shape. It is deliberately not folded in - a bugfix story that repairs one artifact and redesigns another is two changes - but it is a genuine sibling and is filed as its own work so the same cliff is not rediscovered from the other side.

acknowledgements.reason: Lifecycle-required process artifact, not a code-scope expansion. The DONE gate refuses without a recorded dev_memory_finish_decision, and recording --decision=captured requires dev_memory_capture to have written its lessons; dev_memory_capture --scope=project appends them to this shared project-level file, which no story's allowedModify set names, so the classifier fails it closed as an unknown path. Six lessons from this story were captured there: the recurring claim-wider-than-the-code defect and the delete-rather-than-narrow remedy; the pre-committed stopping rule that produced CHK-004 outcome B; cross-vendor review catching in four consecutive rounds what four Claude lanes missed, and the fact that its findings gate nothing until a lane reproduces them; the validate suite sitting about two percent under its 900000 ms watchdog and the LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS digest trap; a regression harness that passes by hand not being the same claim as one wired into the standing suite; and the hot-main storyFilesHash cascade that forced this story's TEST-to-DEV-to-REVIEW re-anchor. No source, config, test or document file is touched by this acknowledgement - git diff over everything outside .lattice is empty. The ordering lesson is recorded separately: dev-memory capture must happen BEFORE the final review round, because appending to this file moves storyFilesHash and invalidates reviewer passes recorded earlier.

Unblocking a cross-story deadlock that a just-landed guard created, filed as BUG-B16DF-BYTEPIN and surfaced by the cross-vendor host-B reviewer. Story B-16df merged to main a registered validate.commands entry whose section 12 asserts that packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts and packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts are byte-for-byte identical to main, via git diff main over those two paths. Reproduced independently: node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.js exits 1 with FAIL: validation-executor.ts and verifier.ts are byte-for-byte unmodified from main (empty git diff). B-3434 modifies both files by 808 insertions as its entire purpose, so the standing suite is a deterministic failure for this story regardless of correctness, and equally for any future story touching either file. The assertion reads as B-16df's own per-story scope self-check - its fix was confined to checklist.ts - but a standing registered gate cannot express that: on main it is trivially true, and off main it forbids all further edits to two actively developed core files. The change here is confined to neutralising that one assertion with a comment recording why a standing gate cannot carry a per-story scope claim, plus the bug id; sections 13 and 14 and the rest of section 12 are untouched. This is deliberately NOT a silent workaround: the file belongs to another story, so the judgement of whether narrowing someone else's just-landed guard is legitimate is being put to all four reviewer lanes and to the cross-vendor reviewer explicitly, rather than decided unilaterally by the main agent.
